text:
Marathon Petroleum rose 2.6% today as crude oil prices spiked to their highest level in six weeks following escalating military tensions in the Middle East—Iran and the U.S. traded strikes over the weekend, and Houthi forces reportedly attacked Saudi energy facilities. For a refiner like Marathon, higher crude prices can actually boost profitability when refineries are running at full capacity (98% utilization today) because they can sell refined products at prices that don't fall proportionally with the crude cost increase, a dynamic known as the refining margin.

The stock's broader 10% jump over two weeks reflects confidence in refining economics as geopolitical risk keeps oil elevated while U.S. refinery capacity remains maxed out and storage levels sit comfortably, signaling steady demand for refined fuels without supply gluts.
